action.action-desc: Mr. Carper (for himself and Mr. Merkley) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
Reported by Mr. Johnson, with amendments
action.action-instruction: Omit the part struck through and insert the part printed in italic

form.official-title: To amend title 5, United States Code, to require the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to establish and maintain a public directory of the individuals occupying Government policy and supporting positions, and for other purposes.

subsection.text: This Act may be cited as the Periodically Listing Updates to Management Act of 2020 or the PLUM Act of 2020.
The purposes of this Act are to—

paragraph.text: modernize the practice of publishing the Plum Book, which has occurred nearly every 4 years since 1952, and contains data on more than 9,000 Federal civil service leadership and support positions in the legislative and executive branches of the Government that may be subject to noncompetitive appointment;
enhance transparency by reporting who is serving in the Government and making policy decisions; and
improve the frequency, accuracy, and accessibility of data on the individuals filling Government policy and supporting positions.

section.header: Establishment of public website on Government policy and supporting positions

paragraph.text: Subchapter I of chapter 33 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

section.header: Government policy and supporting position data

paragraph.text: The term agency means—

subparagraph.text: any Executive agency, including the United States Postal Service and the Postal Regulatory Commission;
the Architect of the Capitol, the Government Accountability Office, the Government Publishing Office, and the Library of Congress; and
the Executive Office of the President and any component within that Office (including any successor component), including—

clause.text: the Council of Economic Advisors;
the Council on Environmental Quality;
the National Security Council;
the Office of the Vice President;
the Office of Policy Development;
the Office of Administration;
the Office of Management and Budget;
the Office of the United States Trade Representative;
the Office of Science and Technology Policy;
the Office of National Drug Control Policy; and
the White House Office.

paragraph.text: The term appointee—

subparagraph.text: means an individual serving in a policy and supporting position; and
includes an individual serving in a policy and supporting position temporarily in an acting capacity in accordance with—

clause.text: sections 3345 through 3349d (commonly referred to as the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998);
any other statutory provision described in section 3347(a)(1); or
a Presidential appointment described in section 3347(a)(2).

paragraph.text: The term covered website means the website established and maintained by the Director under subsection (b).
The term Director means the Director of the Office of Personnel Management.
The term policy and supporting position means—

subparagraph.text: a position that requires appointment by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate;
a position that requires or permits appointment by the President or Vice President, without the advice and consent of the Senate;

a position occupied by a limited term appointee, limited emergency appointee, or noncareer appointee in the Senior Executive Service, as defined under paragraphs (5), (6), and (7), respectively, of section 3132(a);
a position of a confidential or policy-determining character under schedule C of subpart C of part 213 of title 5, Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor regulation;
a position in the Senior Foreign Service;

any career position at an agency that, but for this section and section 2(b)(4) of the PLUM Act of 2020, would be included in the publication entitled United States Government Policy and Supporting Positions (commonly referred to as the Plum Book); and

any other position classified at or above level GS–14 of the General Schedule (or equivalent) that is excepted from the competitive service by law because of the confidential or policy-determining nature of the position duties.

paragraph.text: The term policy and supporting position—

subparagraph.text: means any position at an agency, as determined by the Director, that, but for this section and section 2(b)(4) of the PLUM Act of 2020, would be included in the publication entitled United States Government Policy and Supporting Positions (commonly referred to as the Plum Book); and
may include—

clause.text: a position on any level of the Executive Schedule under subchapter II of chapter 53, or another position with an equivalent rate of pay;
a general position (as defined in section 3132(a)(9)) in the Senior Executive service;
a position in the Senior Foreign Service;
a position of a confidential or policy-determining character under schedule C of subpart C of part 213 of title 5, Code of Federal Regulations, or any successor regulation; and

any other position classified at or above level GS–14 of the General Schedule (or equivalent) that is excepted from the competitive service by law because of the confidential or policy-determining nature of the position duties.

subsection.text: The Director shall establish and maintain a public website containing the following information:

paragraph.text: Each policy and supporting position in the Federal Government, including any such position that is vacant.
Each individual who—

subparagraph.text: is serving in a position described in paragraph (1); or
previously served in a position described in paragraph (1) under the President then in office.

subsection.text: With respect to any policy and supporting position listed on the covered website, the Director shall include—

paragraph.text: the agency and agency component (including the agency and bureau code used by the Office of Management and Budget) in which the position is located;
the name of the position;
the name of the individual occupying the position (if any);
the geographic location of the position, including the city, State or province, and country;
the pay system for the position;
the level, grade, or rate of pay;
the term or duration of the appointment (if any);
the expiration date, in the case of a time-limited appointment;
a unique identifier for each appointee to enable tracking the appointee across positions; and
whether the position is vacant.

subsection.text: The Director shall make the data on the covered website available to the public at no cost over the internet in a searchable, sortable, downloadable, and machine-readable format so that the data qualifies as an open Government data asset, as defined in section 3502 of title 44.

paragraph.text: Each agency shall provide to the Director any information that the Director determines necessary to establish and maintain the covered website, including the information uploaded under paragraph (4).

Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of the PLUM Act of 2020, the Director shall issue instructions to agencies with specific requirements for the provision or uploading of information required under paragraph (1), including—

subparagraph.text: specific data standards that an agency shall follow to ensure that the information is complete, accurate, and reliable;
data quality assurance methods; and
the timeframe during which an agency shall provide or upload the information, including the timeframe described under paragraph (4).

paragraph.text: The Director shall identify on the covered website any agency that has failed to provide—

subparagraph.text: the information required by the Director;
complete, accurate, and reliable information; or
the information during the timeframe specified by the Director.

Not later than 90 days after the date on which the covered website is established, and not less than once during each 30-day period2-year period thereafter, the head of each agency shall upload to the covered website updated information (if any) on—

clause.text: the policy and supporting positions in the agency;
the appointees occupying those positions in the agency; and
the former appointees who served in policy and supporting positions in the agency under the President then in office.

subparagraph.text: Information provided under subparagraph (A) shall supplement, not supplant, data previously provided under that subparagraph.

paragraph.text: The Director shall establish a central help desk, to be operated by not more than 1 full-time employee, to assist any agency with implementing this section.

subparagraph.text: The Director shall consult with the 18F office (or any successor office) within the General Services Administration for purposes of the development, establishment, operation, and support of the covered website.
The Director—

clause.text: may designate 1 or more agencies to participate in the development, establishment, operation, and support of the covered website; and
with respect to any such designation, may specify the scope of the responsibilities of the agency so designated.

paragraph.text: Each agency shall comply with the instructions and guidance issued by the Director to carry out this section, and, upon request of the Director, shall provide appropriate assistance to the Director to ensure the successful operation of the covered website in the manner and within the timeframe specified by the Director under subsection (e)(2).
The head of an agency shall include with any submission of information described in paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.text: an explanation of how the agency ensured the information is complete, accurate, and reliable; and
a certification that the information is complete, accurate, and reliable.

Not less frequently than semiannually, the Director, in coordination with the White House Office of Presidential Personnel, shall confirm that the information on the covered website is complete, accurate, reliable, and up-to-date.

On the date that is 90 days after the date on which the covered website is established, the Director, in coordination with the White House Office of Presidential Personnel, shall confirm that the information on the covered website is complete, accurate, reliable, and up-to-date.
On the date on which the Director makes a confirmation under subparagraph (A), the Director shall publish on the covered website a certification that the confirmation has been made.

paragraph.text: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Director may—

subparagraph.text: request additional information from an agency; and
use any additional information provided to the Director or the White House Office of Presidential Personnel for the purposes of verification.

paragraph.text: The Director shall establish a process under which members of the public may provide feedback regarding the accuracy of the information on the covered website.

As soon as practicable after a transitional inauguration day (as defined in section 3349a), the Director, in consultation with the Archivist of the United States, shall archive the data that was compiled on the covered website for the preceding presidential administration.
The Director shall make the data described in paragraph (1) publicly available over the internet—

subparagraph.text: on, or through a link on, the covered website;
at no cost; and
in a searchable, sortable, downloadable, and machine-readable format.

paragraph.text: The table of sections for subchapter I of chapter 33 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

toc.toc-entry: 3330f. Government policy and supporting position data.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall establish the website required under section 3330f(b) of title 5, United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1).

In this subsection, the terms agency, covered website, and policy and supporting position have the meanings given those terms in section 3330f of title 5, United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1).

There is authorized to be appropriated $10,000,000,There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary, to remain available until expended, for developing the covered website under section 3330f(b) of title 5, United States Code, as added by subsection (a)(1).

subparagraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date on which the covered website is established, the Comptroller General of the United States shall conduct a review of, and issue a briefing or report on, the implementation of this Act and the amendments made by this Act.
The review conducted under subparagraph (A) shall include—

clause.text: the quality of data collected and whether the data is complete, accurate, timely, and reliable;
any challenges experienced by agencies in implementing this Act and the amendments made by this Act; and
any suggestions or modifications to enhance compliance with this Act and the amendments made by this Act, including best practices for agencies to follow.

paragraph.text: Beginning on January 1, 2024—

subparagraph.text: the covered website shall serve as the public directory for policy and supporting positions in the Government; and
the publication entitled United States Government Policy and Supporting Positions, commonly referred to as the Plum Book, shall no longer be issued or published.
